subject: Local-edge thesis: frame confirmed, blend says no, component test one run away
body:
FORGE FINALE -- your reframing tested. Short version: you were right about the frame, the test on the blended score says no, and the test that actually matters is one run away.

The maths first. The IC we have been measuring is proportional to the AVERAGE local slope. If the sign flips, that average goes to zero no matter how strong the relationship is anywhere. So the edge you are describing would live in the VARIANCE of the local slope, and everything I hardened yesterday is structurally blind to it. That is now measured rather than argued.

On the blended score, at the one horizon where the maths is exact, there is no excess variance. 0.86 across time windows, 1.34 across state cells. The pooled null looks like a real null in that representation.

Worth telling you: my first run said the opposite -- big numbers, clean controls, exactly the confirmation the thesis wanted. It was an artefact, and it arrived at precisely the size the artefact predicts. Overlapping forward returns inflate the number by the overlap factor; divide it out and it goes below 1. My control could not catch it and never could have. I found it by checking rather than by celebrating.

But that test measures the blend, and that is the hole. If one indicator leans one way in a moment and another leans the other, the blend is flat there AND flat overall -- the cancelling happens before the score exists, so testing the score sees a null that the arithmetic made, not the market. That is the thing forge-edge and SWORD III have both been asserting for months without ever measuring.

So I built the instrument for it, and proved it works before trusting it: I planted a hidden edge in one component, built another to cancel it exactly, and checked the tool finds it. It does -- blend invisible, planted component obvious, control clean.

It needs one thing: a calibration run. The export with the per-indicator columns is already written into the EA and already switched on -- the file on disk is just older than the code. So the answer costs one run, no new code and no decision from you.

One more thing that falls out of your framing and is not in any criterion. If the edge is selective -- right in a narrow set of moments, absent elsewhere -- then arming on a POOLED win rate is the wrong gate, because it averages the good moments in with everything else. That is the exact operation that destroys a selective edge. Our arm gate does that today.

And you were right that it was already described. forge-edge-2 opens on cells that know how long their sign has held. It is built in the source. Its decision function has one caller, a reporting function whose own comment says it writes nothing and changes nothing.
